what_matters.head: Nvidia reports Q3 results after Tuesday's New York close, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress.
what_matters.detail: Results come at about 1:20 p.m. Pacific on 17 Nov (about 05:20 SGT Wednesday), with the call at 06:00 SGT (company 8-K). The company forecast revenue of $108.0B, plus or minus 2%, and a gross margin of 74.0%, plus or minus half a point. 45 analysts expect about $108.7B. Options trading implies a move of about ±8.6% either way by 18 Nov (as of Friday's close).

what_matters.head: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia's board should look outside the company for its next chief executive, and that he wants answers from the board within 10 days.
what_matters.detail: He said on Fox News that 'we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel', and asked whether Nvidia had pushed 'seemingly illicit sales' to lift its revenue (Al Jazeera). Separately, the Financial Times reported on Sunday that Jensen Huang is considering a comeback. Nvidia did not comment (Reuters). None of this is in Friday's US prices.

what_matters.head: The chip fund fell 3.7% on Friday, about 1.1 times its usual daily move. AMD fell 8.8% and Broadcom 4.8%. Cerebras was the exception, up 11.2% after its results.
what_matters.detail: Early buying in AI-chip names reversed into a sector-wide sell-off, and AMD had no news of its own (Motley Fool). This morning in Seoul, SK Hynix was down 5.9% and Samsung 3.5% by 12:05 SGT. Investing.com said investors were cutting AI-related shares before Nvidia's results. The chip fund still ended the week up 9.3%.

after_data.text: The FT reported earlier that the board had approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas (Reuters). President Trump named former Apple chief executive Tim Cook in a Truth Social post (Al Jazeera).
Trading is due to begin on Thursday 19 Nov, two days after Nvidia's results (Reuters). Its 10 Nov filing set a range of $70–78 a share, with pricing expected on 18 Nov.

movers.why: Rose after Thursday's after-hours Q3 results: core revenue up 70% to $230.9M, and a Q4 core revenue forecast of $310–330M against the $271.2M analysts expected (Yahoo Finance).
Fell in a sector-wide AI-chip sell-off that reversed early gains, with no AMD news. It had risen as much as 30% earlier in the week (Motley Fool).
Fell with the rest of the chip group on Friday after a strong week (Yahoo Finance). No Broadcom news was reported.
Fell for a second day after its Q3 results. Baird cut its price target to $200 from $340 and Bank of America to $265 from $310, both citing data-centre delays (24/7 Wall St.).
Fell this morning with Asian chip stocks. Tokyo Electron fell 5.2% and Advantest 10%, as investors cut AI-related shares before Nvidia's results (Investing.com).

latest.tape_note: On Friday the S&P 500 fund fell 0.36%, the Nasdaq 100 fund 1.20% and the chip fund 3.67%. All three rose for the week. The 10-year yield rose 5 basis points to 5.15%. US producer prices rose 0.3% in October against the 0.4% expected, and were 6.5% higher than a year earlier, the largest annual rise since November 2022 (Yahoo Finance). The VIX rose 3.2%. The dollar index rose 0.2% and the US dollar rose 0.1% against the Singapore dollar. US crude slipped 0.2% and gold was flat.

recent.headline: Nvidia reports Q3 results after Tuesday's New York close, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress.
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive and left its board, effective immediately. Nvidia closed down 4.3%, about 1.8 times its usual daily move.
Nvidia fell about 8% after hours on Wednesday, after the Wall Street Journal reported that its board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia fell another 5.5% on Tuesday, about 2.3 times its usual daily move, on twice its average volume. It is down 18.3% over five sessions.
US stocks had their biggest rally in about seven months on Monday: the S&P 500 fund rose 2.4% and the chip fund 7.5%.
